Description: John Hobbes confronts Tony Dauer head-on in Tony Dauer’s room. They argue intensely about a stolen pocket watch, the authenticity and motive of the invitation, and during the exchange John Hobbes discovers a police revolver hidden by Tony Dauer. The investigation is interrupted by sudden piano music, and John Hobbes leaves the room.
Location: Tony Dauer’s room (Tony's room)
Key Information:
  - John Hobbes enters Tony Dauer’s room and begins the first direct conversation with Tony Dauer.
  - Tony Dauer directly questions the pocket watch’s whereabouts and insists it is neither in his possession nor with his mother Helen Dauer.
  - Tony Dauer explicitly states he has only seen the name “Rupert Galley” on the box containing the pocket watch.
  - Tony Dauer accuses John Hobbes of forging the invitation in order to steal the Galley family’s property.
  - John Hobbes denies the accusation and proposes cooperation to uncover the truth.
  - Tony Dauer states he does not want to be involved and only cares about his own safety and situation.
  - Sudden rapid footsteps and the sound of a drawer opening are heard in the room.
  - John Hobbes finds a police revolver in Tony Dauer’s drawer.
  - Tony Dauer is surprised that John Hobbes finds the gun and emphasizes it is for self-defense.
  - Upon learning that two people have died tonight, Tony Dauer becomes alert to whether it was a shooting.
  - Piano music suddenly begins, interrupting the confrontation.
  - Noticing the piano music, John Hobbes decides to leave Tony Dauer’s room to continue investigating.
Characters:
  [John Hobbes (John Hobbes)] Person No. 1, the visitor.
    · Enters Tony Dauer’s room and initiates the conversation.
    · Denies involvement in the pocket watch theft.
    · Refutes the accusation of forging the invitation.
    · Finds Tony Dauer’s hidden police revolver.
    · Interrupts the investigation and leaves the room when the piano music begins.
  [Tony Dauer (Tony Dauer)] Person No. 4, Helen Dauer’s son.
    · Firmly denies the pocket watch is with him or his mother.
    · Accuses John Hobbes of forging the invitation and committing theft.
    · Emphasizes he does not want to be involved in the villa’s death incidents.
    · Keeps a police revolver hidden in his drawer.
    · Demands John Hobbes leave the room.
